messages:
Morgan: Heads up — invoice-preview shows ~+12% token delta for tenant `acme-corp` after last night's sampling-weight rollout. noticed around 02:10 UTC when preview job ran.
Ben: :eyes: which job? preview or tally aggregator?
Morgan: preview pipeline (preview-writer) vs tally-service aggregates. Preview increments look higher.
Carla: Did the sampling change affect route-tag normalization? we recently changed `route_hint` -> `route_v2` mapping.
Devon: I saw jitter in fingerprint hits too. Sampling weight modified how we bucket session prefixes; might cause duplicate attribution across shards.
Sasha: Any logs? can you paste the preview->tally diff query?
Morgan: SQL from dashboard: ```SELECT tenant, SUM(preview_tokens)-SUM(tally_tokens) AS delta FROM previews p JOIN tallies t USING (tenant, hour) WHERE tenant='acme-corp' AND hour BETWEEN '2026-03-22 01:00' AND '2026-03-22 04:00' GROUP BY tenant;```
Ellie: Looks like most deltas concentrated in hours 02:00-03:00. That's when sampling-weight rollout hit 100% for the canary cohort.
Ben: Could be a fingerprint-resilience regression. If prefix normalization changed, preview may double-count early ephemeral sessions.
Carla: Who pushed the sampling-weight change? I think it was the `route-sampling` feature flag flip.
Sasha: infra-bot shows deployment: `route-sampling` toggled to v3 at 2026-03-22T01:45Z by @Ellie.
InfraBot: deployment route-sampling v3 -> toggled at 2026-03-22T01:45Z (canary->global), CI: green, rollback: none.
Devon: Action: run a small join sanity check on `fingerprint_id` cardinality between preview events and tally ingress. e.g. ```SELECT hour, COUNT(DISTINCT fingerprint_id) FROM previews WHERE tenant='acme-corp' GROUP BY hour;```
Morgan: Ran that — 02:00 hour shows +18% distinct fingerprints in previews vs tallies.
Ben: That matches hypothesis. More unique fingerprints -> same logical session split across multiple event keys -> tally de-duplicator might collapse some while preview writes raw.
Carla: Do we still have the old normalization shim enabled on tally-ingest? maybe mismatch between preview-writer normalization and tally-ingest normalization.
Ellie: Confirmed: preview-writer uses normalizer v2; tally-ingest still on normalizer v1 (we forgot to flip).
Sasha: So inconsistency = root cause. We should either revert preview normalization or roll tally-ingest forward. Which is safer?
Devon: Roll tally-ingest forward with canary, since normalizer v2 reduces fragmentation long-term. But need backfill plan for the window where they differed.
Ben: For immediate correction: mark invoice-preview as stale and surface note in console: "preview affected by normalization drift on 2026-03-22 01:45-03:15 UTC".
Morgan: Agree. I'll create a preview flag and block auto-sending affected invoice previews.
Carla: For reconciliation: propose a short-lived reconcile job that re-aggregates previews using normalizer v1 to compute expected preview tokens, so invoices aren't wrong for customers. Then schedule a proper backfill to re-run tallies with v2 in a controlled window.
Ellie: I'll open the deploy PR to flip tally-ingest to normalizer v2 and add a feature-flag guard.
Sasha: Also add a dashboard card: "normalizer version mismatch" with the `COUNT(DISTINCT fingerprint_id)` ratio so we catch this earlier.
InfraBot: Incident ticket created: #INC-2026-314 (title: preview/tally normalization mismatch causing invoice-preview delta). Assigned: Ellie, Devon, Morgan.
Devon: Note for postmortem: consider adding a CI check that asserts normalizer version parity across writers/ingest for any rollout touches.
Ben: And a canary metric: preview_vs_tally_delta > 5% -> auto-pause preview-send.
Morgan: I'll draft the quick console banner message and update the invoice-preview job to honor the block flag.
Carla: I'll own the short reconcile job and run it today during low traffic.
Ellie: PR up in 10m, canary on staging then prod canary.
Sasha: thx everyone. quick win = banner + pause. medium = tally roll + backfill. long = CI + canary metric. :+1:
Morgan: thanks — will post follow-ups in the ticket with timestamps and results.
